article_title: Experiential Course Learning, Wellness, and Higher Education: Qualitative Descriptive Study.
citation: Watson AL, Peterson NE, Thatcher B, Thomas M, Hunsaker S, Hooley C, Erekson D, Simpson A, Snow G, Detrick R. (2026). Experiential Course Learning, Wellness, and Higher Education: Qualitative Descriptive Study. JMIR Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.2196/88642
title: The Reflect-Recognize-Reorient (R3) Cycle of undergraduate wellness learning
description: The R3 cycle is a three-phase model the authors propose to describe the iterative process students reported across themes: reflecting inward on thoughts, emotions, and bodily cues; recognizing recurring behavioral patterns and triggers; and reorienting toward concrete, value-driven forward-looking actions. It is positioned as "a concise synthesis of these findings" and a pedagogical bridge between Kolb's experiential learning cycle and Mezirow's transformative learning theory, extending experiential learning beyond skill acquisition to meaning-making and identity development.
requirements: Requires experiential learning contexts with weekly applied assignments, structured reflection such as journaling, and peer dialogue, as in the sampled wellness courses
constraints: Derived from a single-institution, predominantly female and non-Hispanic White, self-selected sample; the authors state mixed methods, multisite, and longitudinal research is needed before broader generalization of the R3 model or causal inferences can be made
target_learners: Undergraduate students, including nursing, prehealth, and general education electives
target_learning_goals: Meaning-making around stress, success, and self-care
examples: The authors map Phase 1 Reflect to Kolb reflective observation and Mezirow critical self-reflection, Phase 2 Recognize to pattern recognition as a discrete sense-making pivot, and Phase 3 Reorient to actions like scheduling micro-breaks or practicing paced breathing before exams
